articleTitle: Shared Electric Vehicle Systems Based on IEC 61850-90-8: Implementation Proposal and Proof of Concept
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: Urban mobility is a central theme in dis-cussions about city development and quality of life. It refers to the ease and efficiency people move within the urban environment. However, with population growth and increased use of individual transport, we can ob-serve several problems, such as traffic congestion, air and soil pollution, and the emission of greenhouse gases. In this sense, this article proposes a sustainable and shared electric vehicle system based on IEC 61850 standard. The proposal addresses the data modeling of the system components, the communication protocols used, and the functional architecture of the system. We base the SCADA system developed for the solution, the electric vehicles, the charging stations, and all the control, monitoring, and supervision devices involved on IEC 61850, where we use its data modeling to guarantee the interoperability attribute. The proposed charging station charges vehicle batteries from solar panels installed at the station, reinforcing the system's sustainability. We present an implementation proposal with a proof of concept case study through a testbed with SEL 451–2 and SEL 421–3 IEDs, an Omicron CMC 356 test case, a GE Reason S20 switch, and an Elipse E3 software. The results show the proposal is feasible, and the IEC 61850 Standard can achieve our shared electric and sustainable vehicle system needs whit good monitoring, supervision, and control performances.

articleTitle: Communication Latency Assessment for an Interoperability Interface Prototype Applied to Power Converters in Laboratory Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: One of the most vital aspects behind performing laboratory-scale studies on the interoperability of power electronic converters within the scenario of smart microgrids is the implementation of communication interfaces. Having the flexibility to support bidirectional communication technologies and presenting easy configuration settings are usually desired features of such interfaces, mostly because they can be used to emulate different data exchange behaviors, which are commonly targeted on the assessment of how power converters impair microgrid operation. This paper presents the implementation layout of an interoperability interface based on an off-the-self microprocessor platform (i.e., Raspberry Pi model), which can be applied to small-scale microgrid laboratory facilities, in which a local area communication network is used to achieve interoperability among power converters. In addition, an experimental assessment on the communication latency of such interoperability system is presented in this paper, considering a TCP/IP-based communication layout using the IEEE 802.3 protocol. The results show that data packet exchange between two communication interfaces can occur as fast as 0.118 ms, with a maximum latency of 1.173 ms, which is generally attractive to the targeted scenario of study.

articleTitle: HVDC Converter Transformers Protection - Part 1: Signal Processing Aspects
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of commutation failure (CF) in Line-Commutated Converter (LCC) High-Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) technology, which causes distortions in nearby AC system current waveforms. The research analyzes current signal characteristics in converter transformers, assesses how this distortion affects phasor estimation algorithms during transients, and examines harmonic components in short-circuit scenarios. The study employs Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT) techniques and estimates har-monic content. The results reveal that anti-aliasing filters modify the original signal, CFs lead to inaccuracies in phasor estimation, and the introduction of harmonics in the signal may block the trip command issuing for internal faults in conventional transformer protections.

articleTitle: Hardware-in-the-Loop Simulation in Distribution Networks: Frequency Variation
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: The integration of smart grid concepts has been a good strategy for increasing power systems automation, where the activities of all consumers and producers are intelligently and efficiently combined to distribute sustainable, cost-effective, and se-cure electricity sources. Installing small computational units in distribution feeders and active loads provides the technological resources to automate the network in collaboration with conventional protection systems present in substations. Developing these computational units with communication protocol standards and data models ensures system security and interoperability. Their technological innovation presents a challenge that must be addressed. As a result, such computational units should employ Hardware-In-the-Loop simulation as a mechanism to study typical and critical operating scenarios. This study introduces a hybrid technique for simulating transients in distribution systems. This approach offers a powerful combination by merging the fast sampling rate of time-domain models used for voltage and current monitoring with the processing efficiency of algorithms designed for quasi-stationary or steady-state. Tests in a real distribution network under short-circuit conditions demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methodology.

articleTitle: Security Mechanisms for R-GOOSE and R-SV Messaging Over a 5G Network
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: The evolution of power grid communication mechanisms is indispensable in a digitally inter-connected world. The IEC 61850-90-5 standard introduces R-GOOSE and R-SV messaging protocols, expanding communication capabilities from Local Area Networks (LAN) to Wide Area Networks (WAN). However, this transition exposes the systems to heightened cybersecurity risks. This text delves into the security mechanisms inherent in R-GOOSE and R-SV messaging over a 5G network, scrutinizing their effectiveness in mitigating emerging threats. Encryption and digital signatures are examined in detail, with their advantages and implementation intricacies dissected. Through rigorous testing, the impact of these security measures on message transmission efficiency is measured, revealing their temporal implications. This analysis underscores the imperative for robust security measures in substation communication protocols, especially as the intersection of virtual and physical domains amplifies the potential consequences of cyberattacks. In an era where reliable grid operation is synonymous with security, this study serves as a roadmap for bolstering power grid communication's resilience against an ever-expanding spectrum of cyber risks.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Optimization Techniques for Photovoltaic Module Parameter Extraction Using the Single Diode Model
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: The use of solar energy is undergoing rapid global growth, driven by the reduction in solar technology costs. To maximize the efficiency of photovoltaic systems, accurate simulations play a fundamental role. This article addresses the importance of precise parameter extraction from the model of a diode in photovoltaic modules, aiming to ensure accurate simulations of the behavior of these systems. Therefore, the main objective of this article is to explore the effectiveness of various optimization tools in improving the estimation of these parameters, with the aim of enhancing modeling and providing more accurate predictions of the performance of photovoltaic solar energy systems under different environmental and technological conditions.

articleTitle: Inductive Voltage Transformer Model for High-Frequency Studies
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: A wideband black-box model is proposed to represent the transient response of an inductive voltage transformer used in 15-kV class distribution systems in Brazil. The proposed model is used to evaluate the surge transfer characteristics of the voltage transformer considering different loads for the application of a step-like impulse voltage at primary side. The model is built as a Norton-type equivalent circuit that is valid from 10 Hz to 10 MHz. It is demonstrated that the model is able to accurately reproduce the transient waveforms measured at the transformer secondary side for the application of impulse voltages at the primary side in all tested cases.

articleTitle: Analysis of Energy Consumption in Smart Edge Processing Device
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: This work presents an analysis of the energy consumption for a setup developed with embedded artificial intelligence to recognize the characters of an analogic hydrometer and transmitting the data via LoRa. The results showed that the developed device with image edge computing is capable of capturing the image, recognizing the specific characters in the image and transmitting. An estimated battery lifetime is 5 years and 3 months using a battery with a capacity of 10,000 [mAh], based on a daily transmission of 5 characters from the hydrometer.

articleTitle: Analysis of a Wind Speed Prediction Model Based on Decision Trees
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)

authors.preferredName: Leiliane Trindade de A. do Monte

abstract: Predicting wind speed is crucial for efficient wind farm management, aiming to optimize en-ergy production and ensure grid stability. This paper addresses wind speed prediction using data from a LIDAR sensor at five measurement points at different heights (40 to 260 meters). A model based on decision trees, specifically the Random Forests (TreeBagger), has been applied to predict wind speed at 10 to 60-minute intervals. The model's performance has been evaluated using the Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE), and Coeffi-cient of Determination (R2) indices. The point closest to the coast (PO) yielded the best results, with RMSE ranging from 0.15 to 0.22 m/s, MAPE ranging from 0.69% to 1.51%, and R2 of 0.99. As the measurement points moved away from the coast, errors increased slightly due to variations in temperature and surface roughness. Data collection at 10-minute intervals provided a robust model training and evaluation dataset. The evaluation metrics reveal the quality of predictions regarding accuracy and generalization ability. The adopted approach provides valuable information for improving wind en-ergy prediction under specific conditions, as found at the investigated site.

articleTitle: A Photovoltaic MPPT Charge Controller Real-Time Testbed for Cybersecurity Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: The increasing deployment of distributed energy resources (DER) over the last decade is a great ally to combat climate change and strengthen the grid during increasingly common extreme weather events. However, DER systems, combined with the ongoing transition to a digital power grid, also pose substantial cybersecurity threats. One of the most common communication protocols used in DER integration is the Distributed Network Protocol 3 (DNP3), which is known to have many security vulnerabilities. Thus, it is essential to investigate cyberattack behaviors and mitigation on power systems using DNP3. In this paper, we designed and implemented a cybersecurity testbed for a simulated photovoltaic (PV) maximum power point tracking (MPPT) charge controller. Our testbed uses an MPPT charge controller simulated on a Typhoon HIL602+ real-time simulator with a real DNP3 communication connection over TCP/IP, allowing for safe and efficient monitoring and manipulation of data traffic between the simulated hardware and supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) systems.

articleTitle: Porous Soil Effect on Backflashover Analysis of Power Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: This paper investigates the influence of the porosity level on soil resistivity and its impact on the overvoltages generated, including the backflashover rate (BFR), on overhead transmission lines (OHTL) subjected to lightning strikes. For this analysis, the general Archie's form was adopted to model the soil where the power system is located. The lightning currents representing first (FRS) and subsequent return strokes (SRS) strike at the tip of the central tower. Four values of porosity level are employed in this analysis: 2,50, 5,0, 12.5, and 25%. Results indicated that the harmonic grounding impedance (HGI) strongly depends on the porosity level. The peak values of ground potential rise (GPR) increase with the increasing porosity level. The critical current to provoke a backflashover is also determined for each porosity value. Finally, the over-voltages across the upper string of insulators and the BFR are assessed. As the porosity level increases, the critical current grows, which leads to higher overvoltages across the string of insulators and higher BFR, showing the importance of considering adequate soil modeling in the transient analysis of OHTL.

articleTitle: HVDC Converter Transformers Protection - Part 2: Differential Function Assessment
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: This paper will analyze the performance of the differential protection of converter transformers that are part of Line-Commutated Converter (LCC) High-Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) systems in the face of transient distortions caused by these systems in the AC network connected nearby. The study will investigate the behavior of the differential protection during external faults in both the AC and DC systems, during transformer energization, and winding faults. To achieve this, the systems will be modeled in software ATP/ATP Draw, considering the employed control logic. The results reveal that transient distortions occurring in the evaluated scenarios can lead to improper op-erations of the differential protections. This includes non-operation for internal faults due to improper blocking and restrictions caused by harmonics or errors in phasor estimation of currents, as well as improper operations for external faults due to phasor estimation failures in current measurements.

articleTitle: On Improving Differential Protection of Lines Interconnecting Inverter-Based Resources
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: Inverter-based renewable resources, such <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$as$</tex> wind and solar sources, provide a quite different performance during faults compared to synchronous generators. Indeed, their transient response depends on the control scheme established by the grid code requirements, which may lead to traditional protection schemes' misoperation. This paper presents improvements in the differential protection function applied to transmission lines interconnecting inverter-based resources (IBRs) using a current mapping strategy (CMS) on the alpha plane. The performance of the proposed solution was assessed using a wide variety of simulations on electromagnetic transients program (EMTP) software. The obtained results reveal the CMS improves the protection sensibility and leads to a more stable trajectory on the alpha plane, ensuring the dependability and security of the protection system <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$as$</tex> a whole.

articleTitle: Representation of Transmission Lines by State-Space Equations Obtained from the Propagation Function and Characteristic Impedance
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: The objective of this paper is to propose a generic state-space equation representation of transmission lines, based on the π circuit, for the study and analysis of electromagnetic transients in electrical power systems. In this proposal, the line is represented by an equivalent π circuit consisting of discrete circuit elements (resistors, inductors, and capacitors) whose values are obtained from the propagation function and the characteristic impedance of the line. Since it is a model based on discrete circuit elements, the currents and voltages at the terminals of the line can be expressed in the form of state equations, the solutions of which respond directly in the time domain. The model was applied to represent a single-phase transmission line during the energization process and incidence of lightning. The results were compared with the JMarti model, demonstrating that the proposed model was developed appropriately. The advantage of the proposed model is that it is developed directly in the time domain, considering the distributed nature of the line parameters and the frequency effect on these parameters. Another advantage of the model is that it can be easily implemented using any programming language and also in traditional software such as ATP and EMTP.

articleTitle: An Automation System Simulator for Integration of a Hybrid Power Plant: A Real-Unit Case Study
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: This paper describes the implementation of an automation system simulator using low-cost prototyping for testing the communication interfaces and data flow in the automation architecture of a hybrid power plant (HPP) real-unit. The CHESF PV-WF-BESS HPP in study is composed by the insertion of a Photovoltaic System (PV) and a Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) for the hybridization of a Wind Farm (WF) at Casa Nova - Bahia, Brazil. The automation system of this HPP follows a hierarchy architecture divided into five layers: (1) Local controllers; (2) Remote Terminal Unit (RTU); (3) Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition System (SCADA); (4) Plant Information Management System (PIMS); and (5) Intelligence software for power dispatch orders. The simulator structure is obtained using two Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs) Siemens SIMATIC S7 1200, simulating the local asset controllers and RTU in Layers 1 and 2; and two Personal Computers (PCs), representing the roles of SCADA system in Elipse Power, PIMS in Elipse Plant Manager and Application Programming Interface (API) coded in Python, in Layers 3, 4 and 5, respectively. From this system simulator, the integration between the automation layers can be validated, in order to assist in commissioning and implantation stages of the CHESF PV-WF-BESS HPP.

articleTitle: Industrial Control Systems in Environments with Zero Trust Architecture: Analysis of Responses to Various Attack Types
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: The construction of traditional industrial networks poses challenges in cybersecurity, a sindus-tries are increasingly becoming more interconnected for management purposes. In this study, we analyzed events related to the insertion of the Zero Trust approach in industrial control systems. In a simulated test environment, we investigate how these systems respond to cyberattacks commonly observed in industrial scenarios. The results aim to identify potential benefits that Zero Trust policies can offer to industrial control systems vulnerable to cyber-attacks.

articleTitle: Beamforming Design and Analysis of Space Shift Keying for RIS-Assisted Two-Way Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: In the context of sixth generation (6G) wireless communications, this work considers aspects related to beamforming design in a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-aided two-way communication scenario using space shift keying (SSK) modulation. This challenging scenario combines different key technologies with the potential to improve the overall communication rate and efficiency. For that purpose, suitable alternatives for the receive processing and the determination of the RIS reflection coefficients are formulated and analyzed. The results illustrate a comparative performance of the different algorithms.

articleTitle: User Equipment Power Consumption Analysis Under NLOS TDL Channel Models for 5G Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: 5G networks emerge as a solution for many cellular mobile communication scenarios, demanding new energy consumption requirements. Diverse approaches regarding the base station (BS) have already been discussed in the literature, but little has been debated about the user equipment (UE). In this paper, the objective is to understand in practice how much propagation channels subject to multi-path fading can influence the battery consumption of mobile devices connected to a 5G network. Considering an emulated network in the laboratory, 3GPP NLOS TDL channel models and conditions with different resources allocation are analyzed. Results have shown that the poorquality channel requires more power from the battery due to a more complex process for demodulating the degraded Physical Downlink Shared Channel (PDSCH) signal and more energy for sending uploading content related to the Physical Uplink Control Channel (PUCCH). Furthermore, fading profiles with longer delays proved to be higher energy consumers.

articleTitle: Sensitivity Analysis for Neutral Reactor Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: This paper presents an approach for choosing neutral reactors in transmission lines (TL) with shunt compensation. Data from the Brazilian Power Grid were used for digital simulations with ATPDraw, and a sensitivity analysis was carried out with various parameters (line length, neutral reactor, fault location) to find curves that correlate the optimum reactor value with the transmission line shunt compensation level. The influence of line length and compensation level are discussed. Limitations are presented, and the results show that the approach allows reactors to be obtained efficiently for most of the compensation range.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the Use of High-Frequency Currents in Measuring the Grounding Resistance of Substation Grounding Grids
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: The use of high-frequency currents (25kHz) for measuring grounding resistance has emerged as an option to overcome the difficulty posed by connecting overhead ground wires to the ground grid of a substation. However, its use can introduce significant errors into the results, a condition that has been relatively underexplored. In this regard, electromagnetic coupling between the measurement circuit cables is highlighted. Thus, in this paper, an evaluation of the influence exerted by this coupling is conducted, with field measurement data presented. The measurements were carried out at low (80Hz) and high-frequency (25kHz). Additionally, the influence of coupling is assessed through simulations, considering both small and large-scale grids, and its relevance becomes evident.

articleTitle: Minimization of Ground Stations Distribution that Maximizes LEO Satellite Link Coverage Over Any Given Territory
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: The problem of base station placement is long discussed in various fields. However, little work can be found in maximizing a territory coverage while minimizing the number of stations, especially regarding satellite communication. This paper presents a technique to solve the problem of optimal placement of ground stations. It is proposed a multi-step process starting from a constraint relaxed Convex Optimization, then going to a Sequential Least Squares Optimization and a Differential Evolution Algorithm for fine solution tuning. The advantage of the proposed scheme is a trade-off between the number of antennas and the covered area.

articleTitle: Influence of Vertical Wind Shear on the Annual Energy Production of a Coastal Region in Northeastern Brazil
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: Wind has characteristics that are not captured by standard models, and variations in wind flow can cause a significant difference between expected and actual energy production at some power plants. Given the Brazilian wind potential and the need to understand the impact of micrometeorological phenomena on wind turbine performance, this paper presents a comparative analysis of the Annual Energy Production determined by two different methods: using Hub Height Wind Speed (HHWS) and using the Rotor Equivalent Wind Speeds (REWS). These two predictions are compared and their differences investigated taking into account the local micrometeorological phenomena that cause variations in the wind flow, such as atmospheric stability and wind shear. Results demonstrate that the HHWS can overestimate the REWS method up to 30<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, specially in regions where there is significant diurnal variability of wind shear.

articleTitle: Design and Application of an Antenna for Non-Invasive Monitoring of Partial Discharges in High Voltage Equipment
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: In this paper, we present the design and application of a Printed Monopole Antenna (PMA) specifically for detection of partial discharges in high-voltage equipment. To achieve this goal, the antenna had to be designed to operate in the appropriate frequency range, which spans from 0.3 to 1.5 GHz, within the UHF range. Conventional microstrip antennas typically have a narrow bandwidth, so we applied the truncated ground plane technique to expand the available frequency range. Additionally, a series of structural tests and modifications were performed through simulations to enhance the antenna bandwidth. Finally, laboratory tests for partial discharge detection were conducted. For this purpose, three types of test objects were used as sources of partial discharges: oil cell, potential transformer (PT) and insulator. The antenna successfully detected the electromagnetic wave pulses emitted by the partial discharges, as verified through comparisons between the developed antenna and the conventional method (IEC60270) for partial discharges measurement.

articleTitle: Using Reduction Techniques to Obtain a Minimal Consistent Data Set for Training Artificial Neural Networks for Fault Identification Problems
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)

authors.preferredName: João R. M. Soares De Souza

abstract: This work evaluates methods to reduce the size of training data sets for artificial neural networks (ANN) learning, focusing on power systems problems such as fault identification in transmission lines. Usually, many simulations must be performed to obtain a training data set that is representative enough. Furthermore, the training data set is usually composed of elements generated by moving windows. So, each simulation can generate several elements, thus leading to a large data set that could make the ANN training and testing time-consuming. Therefore, using techniques to reduce the size of this training data set while keeping it representative is desirable. Three techniques that could be used for this purpose are presented and the steps to their use are detailed. Time-domain simulations considering random values for all parameters related to transmission line faults are performed to achieve statistical robustness for the results. The results show that the k-means-based technique presented a good performance while keeping mean errors and standard deviations slightly greater than the original condition for the fault classification problem. These promising results suggest the study of other techniques and cases to better understanding and improvement of the procedures.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Transients in Medium Voltage Networks with Realistic Load Modeling and their Impact on Power Quality
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: This paper presents the impacts of various electromagnetic disturbances on the quality of energy delivered to end consumers through simulations in EMTP software. It utilizes both linear load models and models based on EMT components within a realistic distribution system in Brasilia, Brazil. The obtained results are analyzed from the perspective of the ITIC curve to classify which electromagnetic disturbances are capable of producing overvoltages with sufficient amplitude and duration to potentially cause damage to electronic equipment. This aims to characterize the existence of causality relationship, defined <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$as$</tex> the condition for the electric utility's compensation to the end consumer due to equipment damage. Furthermore, it emphasizes the need for realistic load modeling based on EMT components in the study of overvoltages that may cause electrical damage to low-voltage consumer equipment.

articleTitle: On the Performance of Concrete Foundations as Natural Grounding Electrodes in Transmission Line Towers
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: The purpose of this study is to analyze the behavior of the structural foundation of transmission line towers as a grounding system. Using the Segmentation-Integration method implementation available in industry-standard software, a typical tower structure is analyzed under different scenarios, with a compreheensive assessment of current distributions, GPR, touch and step voltages for different values of concrete electrical resistivity, considering a non-homogeneous soil. The results show that in soils with two layers, if the resistivity of the top layer is lower than of the bottom layer, then the tower foundation grounding performance may become impaired, depending on the characteristics and humidity state of the concrete. However, the association of counterpoise conductors with the foundation shows satisfactory results. If the top soil layer has a higher resistivity than the bottom layer, the foundation itself may be sufficient to ensure effective grounding dispersion.

articleTitle: Operation Analysis of an Islanded Microgrid with a Single Wind Power/BESS Generation Unit
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: Generation and load demand disparities that may occur during the islanding of a microgrid result in voltage and frequency fluctuations that cannot be mitigated by the generation if it is converter-interfaced to the loads. Existing literature describes strategies aimed at improving the ability of microgrids to regulate voltage and frequency, relying primarily on Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS). These BESS systems can provide or absorb energy during imbalances, helping to reduce voltage and frequency fluctuations. When a hybrid unit is composed by PMSG-based wind turbine and BESS, the control system for the rectifier and boost converter connected to PMSG operates with Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT), while the bidirectional BESS converter controls power via power balance between wind generation and the microgrid's load; the Voltage Source Inverter (VSI) with droop control handles the grid interface with a grid-forming strategy in islanded mode. In this paper it analyzes the overall system performance, focusing mainly on the BESS drive system's ability to adapt power to unbalances between wind turbine and loads, thus encompassing test variations in wind speed and load. The simulations were performed in the MATLAB/Simulink environment, and the results indicate that this control approach effectively regulates the voltage and frequency levels.

articleTitle: Investigation of Capacitor Influence in the Impact Factor Index Estimation Due to Voltage Sags and Swells in Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: Currently, electrical utilities must constantly evolve, adapt, and seek ways to achieve power quality goals, and to avoid fines for non-compliance with new standards established by government regulatory bodies. This paper investigates how capacitors affect the power quality index called Impact Factor. This index is used by the Brazilian regulator to quantify the severity of Short Duration Voltage Variation (SDVV), i.e., voltage sags and swell, in users connected to the distribution system. Moreover, this paper proposes the application of a stochastic methodology for the estimation of the Impact-Factor index (IF) for each user taking into account capacitors. The proposed methodology is applied to the IEEE 34-node test feeder network. The results show that the strategic installation of capacitors leads to important reductions in the Impact-Factor index. This investigation allows electrical utilities to identify proper capacitors to improve the quality of services without the need for long measurement periods.

articleTitle: Analysis of Complementary Wind Power Plants in Bulk Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: This paper proposes an investigation of the operating conditions of the electric system concerning the voltage levels at the buses and active power flow in the lines in a growing scenario of penetration of wind sources with spatio-temporal complementarity characteristics. This analysis considers the integration of correlated wind farms and investigates how the arrangement of complementary wind plants can mitigate the effects of fluctuations in the electrical system. The investigation applies the load flow analysis of the IEEE 57 Bus system, considering growing scenarios of wind plants integration in the states of Maranhão, Cearã, Bahia, and Rio Grande do Sul with correlated generation data. The generation and load values were obtained through the operation reports of the Brazilian Independent System Operator. To quantify these effects, the indicators of violations in voltage levels and power flow limits in the lines, the PIV and PIMW, respectively, already presented in the literature, have been used. As a result of this investigation, it has been identified that scenarios with arrangements of complementary wind plants from the spatio-temporal point of view are capable of minimizing violations in the operating parameters of the electric system.

articleTitle: Design of a Passive UHF/UWB Tag for Vital Signs Measurement
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: In this research paper, we introduce the conceptualization and development of a passive tag specifically designed for the continuous monitoring of both heart rate and respiratory rate. Notably, this circuit operates by harnessing energy from the UHF (Ultra High Frequency) frequency band. Additionally, a UWB (Ultra-Wideband) transmitter is employed to efficiently transmit the collected health-related data. The implementation of this technology in a compact form factor is noteworthy, as the occupied area of the circuit measures 2.75 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$mm^{2}$</tex>. This design was achieved using the TSMC 180 nm technology, demonstrating the feasibility of integrating advanced health monitoring capabilities into compact and efficient electronic systems.

articleTitle: Electric Vehicle SOC Estimation on the Roads of Large Cities Employing Traffic Co-Simulation and Real Mobility Data
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: Penetration of Electric Vehicles (EVs) in most parts of the planet is still developing. However, the increase in the fleet can have consequences, not only for the electrical grid but also for transport and communication. From the point of view of energy planning, the typical dynamism of EV loading can impose bottlenecks, especially at the distribution level. In this sense, the battery's State of Charge (SOC) is a variable of interest and very sensitive to the driver's behavior. Thus, this work proposes to determine the SOC of EVs on the roads in large cities where electromobility simulations feed an algorithm integrated into a geographic information system. Six different scenarios are considered where heat maps and sensitivity analyses show how the proposal can be used to estimate locations likely to receive charging demand.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Restricted Earth-Fault Transformer Differential Protection Schemes Through an Experimental Test Bench
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: This paper presents an experimental test bench for generating events and faults in a three-phase transformer assembled in a laboratory for the purpose of validating performance of two restricted earth-fault (REF) differential protection algorithms: a conventional method, based on phasors; and a high-frequency-components-based algorithm, which uses the wavelet transform. The high-frequency-based method performed well, detecting all faults rapidly, whereas the phasor-based method failed to detect the fault during a transformer energization event, besides to presenting greater delays than wavelet-based one. The results indicate the feasibility of the experimental test bench in generate representative cases to the validation of existing restricted earth-fault transformer differential protection schemes.

articleTitle: Distributed Generation Hosting Capacity Evaluation for Distribution Systems Through an Optimal Power Flow
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: In this paper, a methodology is presented to determine the maximum hosting capacity (MHC) of photovoltaic (PV) distributed generation (DG) in three-phase distribution systems. To reach this objective, an optimization problem is formulated to maximize the insertion of DG, considering restrictions related to the voltage magnitudes in the system buses, electrical losses, and power flow reversal in the substation. Aiming at validating the proposed methodology, tests are performed on the IEEE 13 bus test feeder in different scenarios, so it was possible to evaluate the results and analyze the optimization method of the software used. The results found are in line with expectations, since the MHC increased as the electricity demand increased, in addition to the voltage profile improving and reaching its upper limit defined by regulatory agencies.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Impact of Integrating Photovoltaic Solar Generation on the Reliability of Distribution Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: To understand the impacts related to the widespread dissemination of Distributed Energy Resources (DER) on the reliability of distribution systems, we elaborated and applied a methodology for assessing the reliability of distribution systems with the presence of Solar Photovoltaic Generation (PV). Therefore, the estimation of the indices the System Average Interruption Frequency Index (SAIFI), the System Average Interruption Duration Index (SAIDI), the Consumer Average Interruption Duration Index (CAIDI), the Average Service Unavailability Index (ASUI), the Average Service Availability Index (ASAI), the Energy Not Supplied (ENS) and the Average Energy Not Supplied (AENS) will be carried out by means of the Sequential Monte Carlo Simulation (SMCS) technique, considering eleven penetration levels of PV. The methodology is validated through studies executed on a modified test system, based on the IEEE RBTS Bus-6. From the case study, it can be observed that the system reliability is enhanced by utilizing the PV system, but the expected improvement in reliability indices is directly linked to islanding operations. The main contributions of this work are: i) in addition to transmission lines and transformers, the failure rates of circuit breakers are considered; and ii) solar radiation varies stochastically.

articleTitle: Assessment of Different Frequency-Dependent Line Models for EMT Simulations of HVDC Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive as-sessment of four transmission line models available in the Alternative Transients Program (ATP)/ATPDraw: Bergeron, classic J. Martí, vector-fitting-enhanced J. Martí and the Universal Line Model (ULM), focusing on the Madeira River HVDC ± 600 kV bipole in Brazil. A benchmark model, based on rigorous earth formulations and transients computations using the numerical Laplace transform (NLT), allows for detailed analysis across various frequencies. Key findings include the inadequacy of Bergeron model beyond the fundamental frequency, superior accuracy of ULM over a wide spec-trum range, and acceptable accuracy of both J. Martí approaches at higher frequencies. Notably, the J. Martí model requires careful evaluation of frequencies near DC.

articleTitle: Parametric Analysis of Phasor-Based Fault Location Methods Applied to Inverter-Based Resource Interconnection Lines
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: This paper presents a case-study-based quantitative analysis that aims to highlight the impact of Inverter-Based Resources (IBR) on six phasor-based one-terminal fault location methods. To do so, a typical system topology to interconnect IBRs to the transmission system was modeled in PSCAD software, and various contingencies on the interconnection line were simulated. Besides fault parameter variations, the assessments consider different IBR topologies, namely Full-Converter and Doubly-Fed Induction Generators, including variations in converter control schemes. After obtaining a representative set of scenarios for the evaluations, the performances of fault location methods were assessed using MATLAB software. Based on these performance studies, recommendations are made on the methodologies that return the lowest percentage of errors when applied to IBR interconnection lines.

articleTitle: Influence of PLL Techniques on Immunity Tests and Islanding Detection of an Inverter-Based Generator
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: Distributed Generation (DG) reached levels of more than 23 GW in Brazil in Sep. 2023, raising concerns about islanding detection and undesirable disconnections. Inverter-based generators (IBGs) must comply with immunity and islanding tests according to technical standards. This study evaluates the impact of three types of Phase-Locked Loops (PLLs) on IBGs, with passive Unintentional Islanding (UI) detection techniques and the active technique General Electric Frequency Scheme (GEFS), using time-domain signal analysis and settings map. It examines whether IBGs with these PLLs may fail to meet immunity and is-landing detection requirements. It is identified that PLL techniques significantly influence immunity tests, requiring precise time delay on protection functions if Rate of Change of Frequency (RoCoF) protection is enabled.

articleTitle: Sum-Rate Maximization in Beyond 5G Systems with Limited NTN Backhaul
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: With the technological advance of fifth generation (5G) mobile networks and the need to increase coverage for this system, it has driven researchers and industry in the search for alternatives for the integration of current mobile networks with the legacy system. At this point non-terrestrial networks (NTNs) arises as a promising technology since geostationary earth orbit (GEO) and low earth orbit (LEO) satellites can provide connectivity in remote regions, on the high seas and even in natural disaster situations. In this context, we investigate the sum-rate problem subject to limited NTN backhaul capacity. Due to problem is nonlinear, we convert it to an integer linear programming (ILP), where the optimal solution can be obtained by standard techniques. The results obtained through simulations show that the proposed solution achieve a higher data rate using less power than the solution using equal power allocation (EPA).

articleTitle: Time-Domain Analysis of Protection Systems - Assessing the Behavior of Overcurrent Function of Harmonic Filters During Energizations
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: This paper evaluates the behavior of harmonic filters subjected to overcurrents during energization. Statistical studies were carried out in ATPDraw considering different techniques to estimate the magnitude of inrush currents, one based on a true RMS estimator and another based on a 60-Hz Fourier filter phasor estimator. The results show that the theoretical limits of the currents used as reference to the overcurrent protection settings presented in literature were consistently defined in the evaluated cases, but that the selection of the decay time could be improved.

articleTitle: Towards to Beyond 5G Virtual Environment for Cybersecurity Testing in V2X Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communication has an essential role for enhancing safety, effi-ciency, and overall driving experience of autonomous driving. To meet the requirements of autonomous driving, V2X demands high data-rate connectivity, per-ceived zero-latency, and high reliability. These char-acteristics are inherently linked to future-generation mobile communication technologies, such as Beyond 5G (B5G) also known as 6G. However, current so-lutions for simulating 5G communications lack inte-gration between the user and control planes, making the simulation not reliable since the 5G control plane functionalities are not taken into account. In this sense, this paper proposes a first contribution towards to the platform called Beyond 5G Virtual Environment for Cy-bersecurity Testing in V2X Systems (B5GCyberTestV2X) by integrating the 5G control plane from Open5GS and UERANSIM into the Simu5G simulator. The inclusion of the control plane in 5G urban mobility simulations increases the security and reliability of the V2X commu-nication service. Therefore, in order to show the impact of the 5G control plane, we validate a simulation with a scenario in the presence of a spoofer transmitting false warning information. As shown in our simulation, the 5G control plane does not allow the connection of the spoofer into 5G network, making the cybersecurity tests of 5G-based V2X communication more realistic.

articleTitle: Enhancing Smart Building Security: Decentralized App Implementation with Blockchain Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: With the recent advancements in the field of internet-of-things (IoT) and artificial intelligence, smart buildings are gaining popularity. Smart buildings play an essential part in offering an upscale atmosphere with lower energy usage and environmental concern in today's modern living. However, with the increased in consumer interaction with the building through IoT devices, it has open various ports for the intruders or unwanted malicious players to enter into the smart building system. In view of this the paper proposes integration of blockchain technology into smart building for enhancing the security. The paper focuses on the illumination/lighting and video surveillance systems by developing a blockchain-based decentralized application (DApp) with smart contracts and a blockchain ledger. The proposed DApp ensures the system security by authentication process with help of private key verification and thus avoids unwanted intruders into the system. For testing the effectiveness of proposed DApp a comparative analysis in terms of gas fees, transaction prioritization, and transaction speeds is presented which offers the users flexibility in balancing cost and efficiency. From the analysis it can be emphasize that the blockchain provides a resilient solution to the challenges posed by the current system.

articleTitle: CNN Architecture Design Impact in DL-Based Channel Estimation Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: This paper presents a trade-off study concerning the impact of convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures design on the performance of deep learning (DL) based channel estimation under orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) systems. Although CNNs have demonstrated remarkable performance in channel estimation, concerns arise regarding hardware implementation due to computation and power consumption limitations, particularly when dealing with limited hardware resources on the network edge. This study investigates the trade-off between the number of convolutional layers, the size and the number of convolutional filters, and the obtained CNN-based channel estimation performance, measured by the mean square error (MSE), error vector magnitude (EVM) and bit error rate (BER). The resource overhead is also analyzed considering the learnable parameters, memory usage estimation, and number of multiply-accumulate (MAC) operations.

articleTitle: Assessing Distributed Energy Resource Hosting Capacity Under Different Grid-Tie Inverter Control Strategies
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: Despite the potential benefits that the integration of distributed energy resources (DERs) can bring to the system, it may cause problems related to power quality constraints, such <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$as$</tex> reverse power flow in substation and overvoltages. An effective approach to address these problems involves the adoption of reactive and active power control in grid-tie inverters associated with DER. Therefore, this paper assesses the impacts of grid-tie inverter control modes, including both Volt-Var and Volt-Watt strategies, on the DER hosting capacity. In order to improve the overall system operation, modifications in the Volt-Var and Volt-Watt curves were proposed. It is noteworthy that these control strategies can have adverse effects on certain distribution system performance indicators, such <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$as$</tex> voltage deviation and power losses; for this reason, these indicators are also evaluated in this study. A stochastic approach was adopted to deal with the uncertainties associated with DERs and loads. Finally, from tests conducted in the IEEE 33-bus test system, it was concluded that the proper adjustment of the Volt-Var and Volt-Watt control curves significantly influences DER hosting capacity, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$as$</tex> well <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$as$</tex> voltage deviation and power losses.

articleTitle: Genetic Algorithm for Base Station Placement in Integrated Access and Backhaul Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: Fifth Generation networks aim to enhance many areas over their predecessor, the Fourth Generation, namely data rate increase, latency reduction, and spectrum usage efficiency. That is achieved through many techniques, such as network densification and the usage of Millimeter Wave, which introduce many new challenges in deployment. In this context, Integrated Access and Backhaul (IAB) technology is meant to increase these networks' flexibility and viability due to its cost-effectiveness, fast deployment, and easy maintenance. In this paper, we investigated the cost-effectiveness of IAB networks in terms of Spectral Efficiency (SE) by comparing, through simulation results, different scenarios with varying quantities of IAB nodes, to a benchmark one containing only Macro Base Stations (MBSs). For this purpose, the network deployment was optimized using a Genetic Algorithm (GA) in order to compare the different scenarios in a fair manner. The results have shown that the introduction of a number of IAB nodes into the network allows us to attain promising cost-efficiency trade-offs, achieving considerably reduced costs at the expense of minor reductions in performance.

articleTitle: Phase Retrieval Based on Supervised Machine Learning Regression Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: This work introduces a novel phase-retrieval technique applicable to different families of sources. The presented approach uses supervised machine learning algorithms to estimate the phase of electromagnetic fields. The methodology involves training the algorithms with a dataset from spherical near-field data taken at multiple sampling locations. The analyses results evidence the efficiency of standard machine learning regression algorithms in efficiently recovering the phase of electromagnetic waves emanating from different sources. Both statistical and numeric validations have been conducted to validate this approach.

articleTitle: Optimal Sizing of Different BESS Technologies in Grid-Connected Hybrid Generation Power Plant
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: This paper presents a novel methodology for the optimal sizing of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) in grid-connected Hybrid Generation System (HGS). It includes a comparative analysis of different BESS technologies and utilizes a centralized dispatch approach to integrate wind and solar power sources. The Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) heuristic is employed to identify optimal solutions, using a curtailment possibility index as a reference. Climatological data from Areia Branca, Brazil, and load profiles from the Brazilian Northeast subsystem are leveraged to assess the impact of BESS integration into the grid. The study is conducted on a modified IEEE 14-bus test grid, resulting in the determination of the optimal capacity for various BESS technologies, specifically 30.25 MWh for Lithium-Ion, 78.85 MWh for Lead-Acid, and 49.75 MWh for Sodium-Ion-based BESS technologies. The results reveal a substantial reduction of up to 16% in fluctuations at the slack bus and up to a 13% decrease in curtailment possibilities.

articleTitle: Comparing Software Supply Chain Protection Approaches
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: Software supply chain attacks are not entirely new. Still, in recent years, a series of relevant high-impact incidents demonstrated they evolved in complexity and have brought them to scrutiny and at-tention. In response, several initiatives concerning pro-tecting against the associated risks formulated frame-works and best practice guides. This study compares some of these initiatives, analyzing taxonomies, threats, and security controls. As a result, knowledge about these initiatives was organized, verifying their simi-larities, and discussing security controls they propose to categorize and understand them. This paper contributes to understanding the subject, suggests ad-vances and future works, and properly identifies controls to prevent incidents.

articleTitle: I-V Curve Tracer Development For The Performance Analysis Of A Photovoltaic Module
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: The photovoltaic (PV) module performance analysis is highly important to evaluate and ensure its health, ir order to achieve a shorter payback. One of the devices capable of verifying the correct operation of a solar module is the I-V curve tracer, as it allows for acquiring detailed information about the electrical parameters of a photovoltaic device. In this work, among the main data extraction techniques, the emphasis was placed on the DC-DC converter strategy, evaluating two topologies, Cuk and SEPIC, to determine which one presents superior performance. After the design of the passive elements of both converters, their operation was validated through simulations using the software MATLAB, employing data from the Kyocera KC200GT solar module under various temperature and irradiance conditions. The results show that the tracers are capable of accurately reproducing the I-V curve.

articleTitle: A Review of IA Use in Education Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: Higher education evasion is a problem that is present worldwide, and that has many consequences to the society as a whole. So, given the importance of this problem, a lot of literature, in the areas of computer science, psychology and statistics, was produced with the intention of predicting and trying to mitigate dropout rates in higher education. Aiming to address this problem this work makes an analysis of the literature about the topic and produce a statistical analysis of a dataset provided by INEP (National Institute of Educational Studies and Research Anísio Teixeira) that brings indicators of dropout of undergraduate courses from universities in Brazil, and a comparison was made with specific data from engineering courses at UNB using two machine learning methods: neural networks and regression. Observing the results of the model made, they show that the model could not surpass the models in the literature, however the analysis carried out revealed interesting data on dropout rates in Brazilian higher education and it is also noticed that dropout increased considerably in the pandemic period. In view of this, predictive models are very useful methods for identifying students at risk of dropout

articleTitle: A Hybrid System Based on Dynamic Selection for Wind Speed Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: In light of the adverse global effects caused by non-renewable energy sources, specifically their contribution to global warming through greenhouse gas emissions, governments are increasing their invest-ments in renewable energy, focusing on wind energy. This study centers on predicting wind speed, an es-sential factor in wind energy utilization, aiming to improve planning and distribution while expediting its integration into the national energy grid. Our proposed approach utilizes a hybrid system that combines a lin-ear autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA) model with machine learning techniques, including Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), Support Vector Regres-sion (SVR), and Radial Basis Function Networks (RBF). We applied this method to hourly and monthly datasets from three cities in northeastern Brazil: Fortaleza-CE, Natal-RN, and Recife-PE. Our approach demonstrated superior performance in all cases when compared to alternative methods. This research offers a valuable tool for enhancing wind energy planning, delivering timely wind speed predictions for various timeframes, thus streamlining its integration into the national energy matrix.

articleTitle: The Role of Spatial Databases for Climatic and Solar/Wind Energy Generation Studies: A Bibliometric Review
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: This paper presents a bibliometric review on spatial databases useful for climatic and solar/wind energy generation studies. Such a type of database has quickly gained importance in various areas of energy and electrical engineering, supporting research and technological advances which require the knowledge of historical climatic data and solar/wind generation capacity. Firstly, works from the literature are analyzed, being statistically evaluated regarding the authors, addressed topics and types of databases. Bradford's Law and Lotka's Law are applied to identify the most relevant journals and authors, allowing to analyze the geographical distribution and distribution per author of scientific production on climatic and renewable generation research. Finally, the most productive authors and countries are identified, being such information used to select the most spread and reliable climatic data and solar/wind databases, whose main features are pointed out, providing a solid foundation for future research and technological developments.

articleTitle: Fault Detection and Classification in Electrical Systems: A Machine Learning and Fuzzy Logic-Based System
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)

authors.preferredName: Paulo S. G. De Mattos Neto

abstract: In order to ensure a continuous and uninterrupted power supply, the detection and classification of faults in electrical systems play a critical role. This paper introduces an innovative decision support system that combines Machine Learning (ML) and Fuzzy Logic (FL) techniques to detect, classify, and diagnose faults within electrical systems. This comprehensive system consists of two key modules: the Classification Module and the Rules Module. The Classification Module utilizes a Decision Tree algorithm to generate a set of rules that enable the accurate classification of the current status of the electrical system. On the other hand, the Rules Module empowers electrical system operators to manipulate this knowledge base, creating more understandable and interpretable rules by employing FL. The results obtained from experimentation using two datasets demonstrate that the proposed system outperforms most of the evaluated classification models and produces more straightforward and interpretable rules. This advancement holds significant promise for enhancing the reliability and maintenance of electrical systems.

articleTitle: Sequential Decoding of Kronecker Codes for URLLC in 5G Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: Kronecker coding is a multi-linear coding technique that offers high adaptability code rate modification and which works well with shorter block lengths, the being an attractive solution for ultra-reliable low-latency communication scenarios present in beyond fifth generation and in sixth generation. This paper presents a new decoding algorithm called multiple least-squares Kronecker factorization decoder, which efficiently exploits the structure of Kronecker code. The proposed algorithm was tested via Monte Carlo simulations, considering Rayleigh and additive white Gaussian noise channels in a single-input-single-output system. For the additive white Gaussian noise channel, the proposed algorithm got a better performance than a low density parity check coding scheme at the same code rate and offered an E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</inf>/N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> gain of nearly 7 dB for a target bit error ratio (BER) of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup>. For the Rayleigh fading channel scenario, a BER of 10–<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> is observed at 16 dB of signal-to-noise ratio.

articleTitle: Statistical Analysis and Modeling of a Quadrotor's Radar Cross-Section
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: This paper focuses on the statistical analysis and modeling of the radar cross-section (RCS) of a DJI Phantom IV drone. The RCS datasets are generated by means of simulations performed at 9.41 GHz for distinct azimuth and elevation angles. Further, these datasets are fitted to usual probability distributions using three criteria, namely log-likelihood (LLK), Akaike information criterion (AIC), and Bayesian information criterion (BIC). Moreover, the impacts of RCS modeling on the radar detection range is analyzed. Based on numerical results, the Exponential distribution is shown to be the best fit for the RCS datasets. A good agreement is obtained between the Exponential's probability distribution function and the histogram of datasets. Finally, the use of this distribution for modeling RCS datasets achieves a maximum error of 3.8% when applied to the radar range equation.

articleTitle: Heterogeneous Ensemble for Multi-Step Solar Irradiance Forecasting in Brazilian's Sites
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)

authors.preferredName: Paulo S. G. de Mattos Neto

abstract: Multi-step solar irradiance forecast is an important part of a successful power grid management. However that forecast can be difficult due to nonlinear patterns and random fluctuation. This work applies statistical and machine learning methods to forecast solar irradiance time series from three different locations of Brazil. The applied models are: Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA), Deep Belief Network (DBN), Extreme Learning Machine (ELM), Multi Layer Perceptron neural network (MLP), Random Forest (RF), and Support Vector Regression (SVR). Taking into account these methods, an ensemble of them is proposed, which has the objective of reducing: the uncertainty of selecting a single model, overfitting, and underfitting. Compared with single models and based on two performance metrics, the ensemble found good overall results when applied in the time series with horizons of 6, 12 and 24 hours ahead.

articleTitle: Channel Estimation in Hybrid-RIS-Assisted MIMO Systems Under Control Link Imperfections
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: Recently, novel architectures for reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) with integrated sensing capabilities have been intensely investigated. Among the different architectures, the so-called hybrid reconfigurable intelligent surface (HRIS) is comprised of hybrid meta-atoms capable of sensing a portion of the impinging signal while reflecting the other one. Due to its signal processing capability, in HRIS-assisted communications, the task of estimating the cascaded channel can be shared between the HRIS and the BS. More specifically, the HRIS is capable of estimating the channel between its panel and the user terminal (UT) while sending such an estimate to the BS via a control link. Upon reception of this estimate, the base station (BS) performs an explicit estimate of the downlink (HRIS-BS) channel. However, in practice, the estimates received via the control link are noisy as a consequence of channel impairments and quantization errors due to limited feedback. This issue may prevent the BS from obtaining an accurate estimate of the cascaded channel and, hence, affects the design of precoding schemes and the overall system performance. In this work, we study the performance of an URIS-assisted MIMO system by considering a more realistic scenario where the control link is not perfect. We discuss to what extent splitting the CSI acquisition between URIS and BS is beneficial, and conversely, in which system setups the estimation of all the involved channels at the BS is preferable.

articleTitle: Enhanced Circuit-Theory-Based Model for Accurate Simulation of Electrically Large Grounding Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: Accurate modeling of grounding systems is crucial in various power systems applications, notably in substation and transmission line groundings. This study introduces a computationally efficient approach for the accurate modeling of diverse grounding grids, incorporating conductor losses in the calculations of leakage current distribution. The paper highlights the limitations of classical equipotential models through simulations, especially in complex, large-scale grounding systems. It quantitatively establishes the conductor length threshold from which the equipotential assumption causes significant deviations from a more accurate model, using parametric simulations with horizontal conductors in uniform soil. The versatile proposed model is further applied to a realistic case accounting for transformer neutral return current, revealing significant discrepancies in touch voltages compared to simplified approaches.

articleTitle: A Deeper Look at Sources of Errors that Affect the Classical Double-Ended Traveling Wave-Based Fault Location Method
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: This paper analyzes sources of errors that typically affect the classical Double-Ended Traveling Wave (TW)-based Fault Location (DETWFL) method. A deeper look at the effects of time synchronization errors, TW detection deviations, propagation velocity in-accuracies and line length uncertainties is provided, being the interaction between these sources of errors also investigated by means of parametric sensitivity studies. The obtained results reveal that time synchronization errors, TW detection deviations and uncertainties on line parameters interact between each other and with fault distance and line propagation velocity, so that, depending on their combination, DETWFL errors can increase or reduce. Hence, the need for two-terminal data synchronization means, reliable TW arrival instant detectors and accurate information on line parameters to calculate propagation velocity settings is proven, being the influence of these factors during DETWFL procedures mathematically explained.

articleTitle: Safeguard URLLC Services in Industry 4.0 Through Reinforcement Learning Scheduling
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
abstract: The potential of Industry 4.0 will be fully enabled through 5G network development. The 5G network functions need to deal with all diversity of applications and their stringent requirements to guarantee the proper function of industrial use cases. When dealing with 5G for industrial scenarios, it is crucial to design resource management functions to fulfill the network slice requirements and protect critical slices such <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$as$</tex> URLLC when required. In this work, we propose a radio resource scheduler for the Industry 4.0 scenario considering three services available: eMBB, URLLC, and mMTC. In this context, we design a reinforcement learning agent <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$as$</tex> an inter-slice scheduler and safe-guard the URLLC slice since it is usually associated with critical applications. The obtained results show that the proposed method obtained better performance in protecting the URLLC slice and also in minimizing the total number of violations to all the slice's requirements.

articleTitle: Organization
publicationTitle: 2023 Workshop on Communication Networks and Power Systems (WCNPS)
